# `facts-plan` fixture — the frozen cooking estate

Everything here is a **copy of the real re-dumped estate** (§8 step 2a) or a
file the landed engine generated from it. Nothing is hand-tuned: when a number
in `expected.json` disagrees with a §7 line, the number stays and the line is
the thing that gets corrected.

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `dump/<spreadsheetId>/` | 17 `dump-workbook` outputs, copied byte for byte |
| `scripts/<dir>/<file>.gs` | the three Apps Script bodies the manifest's cooking rows point at |
| `manifest.json` | the estate manifest, byte for byte |
| `facts/` | the store the run starts from |
| `transcript.txt` | the first 120 lines of `meetings/transcripts/cooking-1405-05-26.txt` |
| `expected.json` | generated by running `facts_plan.build.build` over the above |
| `units/<unit id>.json` | three `facts-unit` documents, the acceptance run's model output |

## The `twin_of` lines

`manifest.json` carries `twin_of` on two rows:

* `fried` → `sokhari` — the two spellings of the fried line («FRIED🍤» and
  «Sokhari») do not fold onto one group key.
* `gozaresh_naharkhoran` → `gozaresh_markazi` — likewise for the two report
  books («Gozaresh naharkhoran», «Gozaresh markazi»).

Without them `plan_units` exits 2, naming both pairs: one candidate would have
to live in two units.

They were this fixture's only hand edit when it was frozen; Task 17 (`a5c529b`)
landed the same two lines in the data repo's own manifest, so this copy is now
**byte-identical to the estate's** and nothing here is hand-edited at all.

## Which workbooks, and why 17 and not 13

The 13 cooking workbooks alone do not reproduce the estate: 30 of the 70
cooking mirror tabs import from four workbooks of other departments, and
without their dumps those 30 edges become `unknown_source` issues (50 edges
instead of 94). So the four sources are frozen too —
`tedade_fooroosh_markazi`, `tedade_fooroosh_naharkhoran`, `anbar_markazi`,
`anbar_shobe_2` — and nothing else. The three `.gs` bodies are frozen for the
same reason: without them the two script rules never mint and the estate-wide
table-reader closure is a different set. With them, the fixture's
`skeleton.json` is **byte-identical** to a build over the whole 28-workbook
estate.

## The store seed (`facts/`)

* `records.json` — the estate's own `units` record (`F-00001`), copied from the
  data repo's committed seed. `apply` refuses any unit symbol no row of it
  declares, so the items' `kg`/`pcs` need it; `build` reads its row keys as the
  run's `unit_symbols[]`.
* everything else is empty, and `.id-seq.json` is at 1 so `apply` does not
  re-mint `F-00001`. The two `place` items a `movement`'s ends must be (v2 §7)
  are minted by the unit that needs them, as `new[]` entries addressed by their
  `N-u-wb-fried-0` / `-1` handles.

## The three unit outputs (`units/`)

Named by the unit id the engine actually mints, which is what `assemble` reads
back off the directory name:

* `u-items-food1.json` — one `keep` per item candidate (137). `##15` («بیکن
  ساندویچ») carries `units[].pack_unit: pack`; nine carry `tracked: false` with
  a reason — mushrooms, sauce, oil, herbs, bread, disposables, the Kentucky
  salad, the mini-Mac bread and packaging, the nine of v2 §17.
* `u-wb-mavade_avalie.json` — the twelve BOM reference records.
* `u-wb-fried.json` — the fried/sokhari line's two night-count records; the
  «موجودی آخر شب» one carries `day_boundary: "01:15"` and the `movement`, whose
  ends are the two `place` items the same document mints in `new[]`.

v2 §17 puts the night-stock record on the **transcript** unit. The engine does
not allow that: §2.3 gives a candidate to its own unit, and
`_build_entries` sends a candidate to `undecided[]` when its own unit returned
nothing, whoever else decided it — and a `new[]` record cannot carry
`medium`/`location`, which are not in `decisionData`. So the record is decided
by the workbook unit that owns it.
